questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention the effects of lesions in Representational Hemisphere?
questions.modelAnswer: • Agnosia and contralateral neglect.
questions.explanation: Lesions in the representational hemisphere lead to agnosia and contralateral neglect.
questions.keyConcept: Effects of lesions in Representational Hemisphere

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Detect site of Area for naming object ?
questions.modelAnswer: • Between the anterior part of the occipital lobe and the posterior part of the Temporal lobe.
questions.explanation: The area for naming objects is located between the anterior part of the occipital lobe and the posterior part of the temporal lobe.
questions.keyConcept: Site of Area for naming object

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Explain Prefrontal Association area initiates and executes plans and motor patterns for expressing individual words?
questions.modelAnswer: • Because it contains Broca's area.
questions.explanation: The prefrontal association area contains Broca's area, which is responsible for initiating and executing plans and motor patterns for expressing individual words.
questions.keyConcept: Prefrontal Association area role in expressing words

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention site concerned with motivation?
questions.modelAnswer: • Limbic association area.
questions.explanation: The limbic association area is concerned with motivation.
questions.keyConcept: Site concerned with motivation

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: What is Amorphosynthesis?
questions.modelAnswer: • Failure of recognition of contralateral side of body leading to unilateral inattention and neglect.
questions.explanation: Amorphosynthesis is the failure of recognition of the contralateral side of the body, leading to unilateral inattention and neglect.
questions.keyConcept: Definition of Amorphosynthesis

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention site of operation of working memory ?
questions.modelAnswer: • Prefrontal Association area.
questions.explanation: The prefrontal association area is the site of operation of working memory.
questions.keyConcept: Site of operation of working memory

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: What are Functions of Wernicke area? Detect it's disorder?
questions.modelAnswer:
Functions:
• Comprehension of thoughts of visual and Auditory information.
• Determination of thoughts to be expressed.
• Choice of proper words to be used.

Disorder:
• Sensory (Fluent) aphasia.
questions.explanation: Wernicke's area is responsible for comprehension of thoughts from visual and auditory information, determination of thoughts to be expressed, and choice of proper words. Its disorder is Sensory (Fluent) aphasia.
questions.keyConcept: Functions and disorder of Wernicke area

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Patient can speak well and has good auditory comprehension but cannot put parts of words together, What is the disorder and it's cause ?
questions.modelAnswer:
Disorder:
• Conductive aphasia

Cause:
• Lesion in arcuate fasciculus (or near the auditory cortex).
questions.explanation: A patient who speaks well and has good comprehension but cannot put parts of words together has conductive aphasia, caused by a lesion in the arcuate fasciculus (or near the auditory cortex).
questions.keyConcept: Conductive aphasia presentation and cause

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: What and Where is Anomic aphasia?
questions.modelAnswer:
Definition:
• Patient finds difficulty in naming seen objects only.

Site / Location:
• Damage in angular gyrus in categorical hemisphere without affecting Wernicke's or Broca's area.
questions.explanation: Anomic aphasia is characterized by difficulty in naming seen objects only, caused by damage in the angular gyrus in the categorical hemisphere without affecting Wernicke's or Broca's area.
questions.keyConcept: Definition and site of Anomic aphasia

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Differentiate between Broca's and Global aphasia regarding Speech?
questions.modelAnswer:
• Broca's aphasia: Speech is slow, hard to come, and limited to 2 or 3 words only.
• Global aphasia: Speech is scant and non-fluent.
questions.explanation: In Broca's aphasia, speech is slow, difficult, and limited to a few words, whereas in Global aphasia, speech is scant and non-fluent.
questions.keyConcept: Difference between Broca's and Global aphasia

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention Sites of Non fluent Aphasia?
questions.modelAnswer:
• Broca's area
• Exner area (Hand skill area)
questions.explanation: Non-fluent aphasia is associated with lesions in Broca's area and Exner's area (hand skill area).
questions.keyConcept: Sites of Non-fluent Aphasia

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text:
Mention cause of Speech disorders in which Speech is:
A) Slow stiff
B) Slow monotonous
C) Stacatto
D) weak breathy nasal
questions.modelAnswer:
A) Slow stiff:
• Upper Motor Neuron Lesion (UMNL)

B) Slow monotonous:
• Parkinsonism

C) Staccato:
• Neocerebellar lesion

D) Weak breathy nasal:
• Lower Motor Neuron Lesion (LMNL)
questions.explanation: Causes of different types of speech/articulation disorders: slow stiff (UMNL), slow monotonous (Parkinsonism), staccato (neocerebellar lesion), and weak breathy nasal (LMNL).
questions.keyConcept: Causes of different speech disorders

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: What is the most common cause of Aphasia ?
questions.modelAnswer: • Embolism or Thrombosis of cerebral blood vessel.
questions.explanation: The most common cause of aphasia is embolism or thrombosis of a cerebral blood vessel.
questions.keyConcept: Most common cause of Aphasia

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: What is Bursting speech ?
questions.modelAnswer: • Hyperkinetic dysarthria due to damage of basal ganglia causing quick involuntary movement.
questions.explanation: Bursting speech is hyperkinetic dysarthria caused by damage to the basal ganglia leading to quick involuntary movements.
questions.keyConcept: Definition of Bursting speech

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention 4 functions of Representational Hemisphere?
questions.modelAnswer:
• Recognition of faces.
• Recognition of musical themes.
• Perception of body orientation in space.
• Identification of objects by their forms.
questions.explanation: Four functions of the representational hemisphere are: recognition of faces, recognition of musical themes, perception of body orientation in space, and identification of objects by their forms.
questions.keyConcept: Functions of Representational Hemisphere

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Explain Hemisphere specialization is related to handedness ?
questions.modelAnswer: • 96% of Right-handed and 70% of Left-handed individuals have their categorical hemisphere in the Left hemisphere.
questions.explanation: Categorical hemisphere localization is related to handedness: 96% of right-handed and 70% of left-handed individuals have the left hemisphere as their dominant (categorical) hemisphere.
questions.keyConcept: Hemisphere specialization and handedness

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention the name of Association area concerned with Creativity, Elaboration of thoughts and Working memory ?
questions.modelAnswer: • Prefrontal Association area.
questions.explanation: The prefrontal association area is concerned with creativity, elaboration of thoughts, and working memory.
questions.keyConcept: Association area for creativity, thoughts, and working memory

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Mention Functions of Categorical hemisphere?
questions.modelAnswer:
• Language
• Logical tasks
• Analytic tasks
• Sequential tasks
• Verbal tasks
questions.explanation: Functions of the categorical hemisphere include language, logical, analytic, sequential, and verbal tasks.
questions.keyConcept: Functions of Categorical hemisphere

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: How Prefrontal Association area shares in control of Emotional behaviour?
questions.modelAnswer: • Through its connections with the limbic system.
questions.explanation: The prefrontal association area shares in control of emotional behavior through its connections with the limbic system.
questions.keyConcept: Prefrontal Association area control of emotional behaviour

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Where is the lesion if the person can still have excellent language comprehension through hearing but not through reading?
questions.modelAnswer: • Angular gyrus.
questions.explanation: A lesion in the angular gyrus causes a loss of language comprehension through reading (alexia) while preserving auditory language comprehension.
questions.keyConcept: Lesion site for loss of reading comprehension with preserved hearing comprehension
